prompt:
References: @image1 is the look of Brenda and the glowing laptop on the coffee table; @image2 is the look of Brenda at the kitchen island with wine, phone face down; @image3 is the look of Brenda reading her phone on the sofa; @image4 is the look of Brenda on her sofa under a blanket; @image5 is the look of Brenda lifting her phone and starting to smile; @image6 is the look of Brenda tapping her phone and grinning; @image7 is Brenda's face; @image8 is Brenda's apartment.
A 28 second cinematic sequence in one apartment on a rainy night, one continuous generation of six shots. Vertical 9:16, ultra-real, ARRI Alexa 35 look, Kodak 500T grain, warm lamp light and cool rain-light through the window, rain streaks on the glass. Brenda's face, hair and clothes exactly as in the references in every shot. Phone and laptop screens always face away from camera; only their glow is seen. No logos, no on-screen text, captions or subtitles.
FRAMING: every shot keeps Brenda and all action inside the middle half of the frame height (the picture will be cropped to a wide band), medium framing, nothing important in the top or bottom quarter.
SOUND: NO MUSIC AT ALL (music is added later). Only rain on the window, room tone, wine pouring, the phone buzzing, the TV murmur, and Brenda's three short lines.
VOICE: Brenda, American, mid-thirties, soft warm mezzo, lazily dry, muttering to herself.
PHYSICS: every object keeps one consistent physical state within a shot; phones and helmets never flip, morph or change shape; no flashes or glitch frames. The phone only ever moves when her hand moves it.
0 to 3.5 s: Brenda on the sofa; the laptop on the coffee table lights up with a notification glow; she glances and flicks it away with one finger, muttered, bored: "Later."
3.5 to 8 s: at the kitchen island she pours red wine; her phone lies face down on the stone, buzzing, its edge glowing; she ignores it and sips.
8 to 11.5 s: she leans on the counter by the rainy window with her glass; the phone buzzes again on the stone; she rolls her eyes without looking at it.
11.5 to 15.5 s: back on the sofa she reads her phone, its glow on her face, a wry smirk; dry and amused: "Nope." She lays it screen-down on the cushion in one clean motion.
15.5 to 21.5 s: she pulls the blanket up to her chin, the TV glow flickering on her face, she settles and yawns; the phone lies dark beside her.
21.5 to 28 s: the phone lights up and buzzes; she picks it up, reads, eyebrows up, a slow smile; playful, giving in: "Ten percent? Fine." She taps the screen once, decisively, grins, and hugs a cushion.
DELIVERY: each quoted line is spoken once, exactly as written, a natural mutter with the emotion in her face and voice. Nothing outside the quotes is ever spoken.
